milestone: Sequential native CPU maps with record elements and record results

implementation.types: Named/anonymous callbacks mapping numeric or nominal finite record elements to numeric or nominal finite record results
implementation.layout: Record outputs use checked target-sized inline storage; numeric outputs retain tensor lowering
implementation.ownership: Existing invocation-owned record arrays, recursive field retention and worker settlement; no runtime ownership changes
implementation.evaluation: Sequential once-per-element callbacks, input length identity preserved, empty inputs execute no callbacks
implementation.limits: Synchronous callback graphs only; Bool/collection-valued callback results, GPU records, escaping closures and record-array fields remain gated

coverage: Named and anonymous numeric-to-record, record-to-numeric and record-to-record maps
All six CPU numerical families; exact integer and floating raw bits, NaNs and signed zeros
Record arrays with nested records, numeric arrays/tensors and immutable updates
Nested callbacks capturing enclosing record parameters and outer scalar values
Empty inputs and skipped failing bodies; nominal type and forged map metadata rejection
Direct/nested workers, repeated cached observations, source settlement and scheduler destruction
Cancellation/deadline/admission failures, malformed field and parent descriptors, allocation failures
No partial publication on failed retention or observation; balanced owner settlement
Imported callbacks, TaskError recovery, executable fault cleanup and preservation of rejected artifacts
Documentation example compiled and executed in all four variants
qualification.scope: Focused regression suite; not the full registered suite

hardware_rerun.reason: Eight Metal tests could not access hardware in sandbox; two frontend assertions still expected record-result maps to be rejected
hardware_rerun.rerun_scope: Only the eight Metal helper tests with hardware access, and the two updated frontend assertions; no compiler/runtime changes after the initial regression run
